confirmed_facts.fact: With the current bridge source, HTTP 200 plus an empty JSON array can only be produced by ProductionEventKitStore.fetchReminders receiving a non-nil empty array from EventKit. Every failure path returns a typed error with a distinct status (401/403/404/405/429/500/504); the gateway transport turns non-array or non-JSON bodies into UPSTREAM_ERROR. Therefore gateway mapping, transport parsing and bridge serialization cannot silently reduce a non-empty list to zero items.
confirmed_facts.strength: strong for the code as read; does not by itself prove which upstream condition produced the empty array

confirmed_facts.fact: AG-07 called reminders_list with list_ids only, no completed/due_after/due_before parameters, so no client-side filter in the gateway could have removed items.
ProductionEventKitStore caches one EKEventStore instance for the process lifetime (cachedStore, created on first request) and never invalidates it nor observes EKEventStoreChanged.
confirmed_facts.strength: strong as a code fact; runtime impact UNPROVEN

confirmed_facts.fact: A nil callback from EKEventStore.fetchReminders is mapped to EventKitBridgeError.timeout (HTTP 504), so a failed query and a real timeout are indistinguishable in the response taxonomy.

confirmed_facts.fact: The bound list identifier still resolves at read time: the 2026-11-10 read returned 200 with source verification PASS, which requires store.calendar(withIdentifier:) to return a calendar whose source matches the registered binding. A fully stale identifier would have produced 404 LIST_NOT_FOUND.
confirmed_facts.strength: medium-strong; a cached EKCalendar object could still resolve a list deleted on the iCloud side, so identity drift is narrowed but not excluded

confirmed_facts.fact: Bridge configuration, including the production gate, is supplied as LaunchAgent EnvironmentVariables and read once at process start. Any gate change therefore implies a process restart, which constructs a fresh EKEventStore on the first request. Every historical read ran on a freshly started process (B3 records service_restarted: true; AG-06 records a reload after the TCC grant).
confirmed_facts.strength: strong; this materially demotes the stale-cache hypothesis

confirmed_facts.fact: BridgeConfig.load() merges the LaunchAgent environment into the config file and the environment wins (`if mergedEnv[k] == nil || empty`). Consequently: when the plist defines EVENTKIT_BRIDGE_PRODUCTION_AUTHORIZED, writing bridge.env has no effect at all; and a value read from disk is not the running process state, because launchd caches the job. A gate operation must therefore be proven by HTTP behaviour plus process identity, never by the file.
evidence: scripts/tests/test_r1_window.sh scenario 12 (plist authoritative source, bootout+bootstrap, 0600 backup)
confirmed_facts.strength: strong as a code fact; the reload semantics of the target launchd could not be measured on this host (see L1)

confirmed_facts.fact: The originally proposed transport was unsafe for a token-bearing request: urllib follows 3xx redirects by default (re-sending the Authorization header to the new location) and honours proxy environment variables, so a redirect or an http_proxy could move the request off the authorized loopback endpoint. The client now builds its opener with an explicit empty ProxyHandler and a redirect handler that refuses every 3xx.
confirmed_facts.strength: strong; both behaviours are asserted offline

limitations.statement: LaunchAgent reload semantics could not be measured on the execution host: `launchctl bootstrap gui/<uid> <plist>` returns `Bootstrap failed: 5: Input/output error` for any job in this environment.
limitations.mitigation: r1_gate.sh detects the authoritative source (launchd_env / config_file / absent), uses bootout+bootstrap for the launchd path and kickstart -k otherwise, then verifies by HTTP status, process identity and a single-key process-environment observation. If both paths fail it exits 4 and writes a failure receipt. The target-host semantics is an execution item in the application (P0), not an assumption baked into the plan.
limitations.residual_risk: On MAC-1, the plist path could still behave differently than the code implies; the window would then fail closed (no gate, exit 11/13) rather than proceed on a false assumption.

hypotheses.statement: The bound list is genuinely empty because no item was ever created in it. Every write path is disabled: bridge is read-only, gateway rejects create/update/remove client-side, and ALLOW_REMINDERS_WRITE_1 was false at the AG-04 baseline.
supporting: no write path exists in any receipt
hypotheses.discriminator: Observe the list in the native Reminders app on MAC-1 under the bound iCloud account, then read it through the bridge.

hypotheses.statement: Items exist in iCloud but never reached the MacServer EventKit local database for this list (account or Reminders sync gap).
supporting: B2 recorded com.apple.Dataclass.Reminders: True, which indicates the dataclass is enabled, not that this list is synced
hypotheses.discriminator: Same observation as H1: an item visible in Reminders.app but absent from EventKit read separates H2 from H1.

hypotheses.statement: The long-lived cached EKEventStore does not observe data written after the process started, so a fresh query against it returns a stale empty result.
supporting: F5 shows the cache exists and is never invalidated
against: F12: the gate is process-start configuration, so every historical read already ran on a newly constructed store; a stale-store explanation would require the store to be stale at process start, which the code does not do
hypotheses.discriminator: Not needed as a separate step any more: the window's read necessarily runs on a fresh process. If a fresh process still returns empty while the native app shows the item, H3 is definitively refuted and H2/H4/H5 remain.

hypotheses.statement: The stored list identifier no longer corresponds to the user-visible list (deleted and recreated), and a cached EKCalendar object resolves the ghost.
supporting: a stale identifier that cannot resolve would 404, and reads returned 200
hypotheses.discriminator: Record calendarIdentifier and sourceIdentifier at read time and compare against the value persisted in bridge.env; a differing identifier in list metadata would confirm drift.

hypotheses.statement: EventKit itself returns an empty result for a calendar that has items (predicate or account-scope defect).
supporting: F3 shows nothing upstream of EventKit can remove items
hypotheses.discriminator: Only reachable after H1/H2/H3 controls pass: item visible in app, fresh store, still zero items.

alternatives_considered.option: C. Defer to the full Seoul/MUSE gateway path
